minutes.headline: Task force reviewed draft stormwater utility fees aimed at a million-dollar budget and agreed to seek a Town Meeting update article.
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force reviewed an EPA-assisted CREATE climate-risk report, a CI update, and draft stormwater utility fee estimates, discussing the residential, commercial and Chapter 90 shares, staffing, and coming MS4 permit requirements. Members agreed to track the figures in a shared spreadsheet and to seek a short, money-free update article for spring Town Meeting. The prior meeting's minutes were approved and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Stormwater Task Force agreed to seek a short, money-free update article on the spring Town Meeting warrant; the warrant closes March 17th.
Members reviewed draft stormwater utility fee estimates and found the residential figure higher than they had expected; no resolution was reached.
Members said they will tell the consultant they do not want residential fees above the annual figure discussed.
Members found the draft funding mix, built from residential fees, Chapter 90 and commercial fees, fell short of the target budget and the draft figures conflicted.
Members agreed to hold off on detailed fee talks with town boards; the first message will be a short teaser without money details.

why_it_matters: A stormwater utility fee would be a new charge on property owners, and the draft shows residential, commercial and Chapter 90 shares that have not yet been settled.

The permit requirements and the staffing built into the target budget are mechanisms that push the fee total up, so the figure residents are eventually asked to vote on may differ from what was discussed here.
The task force plans to bring a no-dollar update to spring Town Meeting, so residents will hear about the utility before they see the numbers.
